newsitem.title: USA: Vertex to study new two-drug AIDS therapy.
newsitem.headline: Vertex to study new two-drug AIDS therapy.

text.p: Vertex Pharmaceuticals Inc plans to study its VX-478 protease inhibitor drug candidate in combination with other protease inhibitors already on the market as part of the emerging two-drug AIDS therapy, Dr. Joshua Boger, president and chief executive officer said.

While most AIDS therapy is currently based on the so- called three-drug cocktail, consisting of a protease inhibitor, along with AZT and 3TC, researchers are beginning to study the effectiveness of two protease inhibitors.

Boger disclosed Vertex' plans Thursday at the Hambrecht and Quist Healthcare Conference, where earlier in the week Agouron Pharmaceuticals said it would also study its Viracept AIDS drug candidate in the two-drug combination.

Boger said Vertex, which developed VX-478 in collaboration with Glaxo-Wellcome will also continue to study other applications of the drug, including as part of the three-drug cocktail. He said VX-478 is easier to use than the protease inhibitors already on the market and has not been found to cause adverse side effects such as nausea, kidney stones and diarreah, associated with some of the other drugs.

He said the company will begin within the next few weeks pivitol trials of VX-478 in combination with AZT and 3TC and also plans to start Phase 2 trials of the drug in combination with each of the three protease inhibitors now on the market. Those are made by Abbot Laboratories, Merck and Roche.
Bertex said it will study its drug in adult and pediatric AIDS.
